answer: Bindings are kept in copper, verified in cipher, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 5 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the ivory check. A farm generating text without memory of its own history therefore fails the binding, which means it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 143 aliases cost 285 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
